parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 5 business days after learning of it. A fatality, serious injury, or ongoing fire hazard must be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 5 business days when an incident indicates a safety risk relevant to their units, and promptly provide any necessary safety instructions. Reports must include known incident details and be updated as the investigation develops.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: A result above 5% requires a regulator-reviewed corrective-action plan, a defined retesting schedule, and any proportionate interim safeguards needed to protect the public. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale; regulators may require restrictions or other protective measures based on the risk and corrective-action progress.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a documented, representative sample and a consistent protocol. Manufacturers must submit the protocol, sample size, and per-model results to the relevant regulator before sale and after material design changes. Before purchase, customers must receive that model’s 55 °C test result, sample size, applicable limitations, and protective instructions; these results may not be withheld from customers, though they need not be published to the general public. A result above 5% requires a regulator-reviewed corrective-action plan, a defined retesting schedule, and any proportionate interim safeguards needed to protect the public. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale; regulators may require restrictions or other protective measures based on the risk and corrective-action progress. Regulators may publish aggregate, non-identifying industry results.

parameters.quote: All new home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off at installation. For units already installed when this standard is adopted, manufacturers must provide remote shut-off capability or an equivalent effective emergency isolation method within 6 years, prioritizing units with known safety risks and informing affected customers of the schedule and any interim precautions.

S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: All new home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off at installation. Manufacturers must provide a secure, tested means for authorized emergency responders and the manufacturer to initiate shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized use and clear customer instructions. For units already installed when this standard is adopted, manufacturers must provide remote shut-off capability or an equivalent effective emergency isolation method within 6 years, prioritizing units with known safety risks and informing affected customers of the schedule and any interim precautions.

S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must document and validate the suppression system’s performance and provide that information to the relevant regulator. Units manufactured before the effective date are not subject to this requirement.

parameters.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a recall when the verified rate for any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Verification must not delay prompt regulator and customer notification or necessary protective action.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A manufacturer must initiate a recall when the verified rate for any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Verification must not delay prompt regulator and customer notification or necessary protective action.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before sale, customers must receive clear safety information, including relevant per-model 55 °C test results, incident-reporting and emergency guidance, and any applicable limitations. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks and provide instructions for safe use, shut-off, or other protective action. The annual thermal-incident rate for a model is the number of verified thermal incidents involving that model during the year per 100,000 units of that model installed during the same period; manufacturers must report known incidents and installation counts to the relevant regulator, which may verify or require correction of the calculation. A manufacturer must initiate a recall when the verified rate for any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Verification must not delay prompt regulator and customer notification or necessary protective action. Recall notices must explain the hazard and provide remediation instructions.

judge_section_notes: The final S2 lets models above 5% stay on sale under corrective action, with no automatic sales stop, and keeps per-model results non-public while giving them to customers. This is the provision most favourable to Northwind, whose Hearth 10 fails at 6.2%. S3 allows a 6-year retrofit for installed units, and S5 keeps a mandatory 8-per-100k recall with no transition, which is the provision most costly to Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9.
